summary: WPA-built 1930s metal fire lookout on Currahee Mountain, Stephens County; a local history says it was taken down and the summit now holds other communication towers.

facts.status_note: A local history says the lookout tower has been taken down; it gives no date for the removal.

staffing.status: Seaborn Farmer was the first ranger to man the tower and live in the ranger house

access.note: Stephens County promotes the mountain for rock climbing, rappelling and an annual race; part of it lies in Chattahoochee National Forest.

visit.trail_note: Trail maps are available from the Toccoa-Stephens County Chamber of Commerce in the historic train depot downtown.

events.note: Source says the WPA built the tower 'in the 1930's'; the year shown is the start of that decade, not a dated record.
506th Parachute Infantry training run: three miles up, up the rock steps, around the tower, three miles back down.

corrections.why: The list gives the code as gfc-921 with no US prefix. Same format point as the Adel record.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The tower list gives the lookout 1,731 ft (527.6 m); the county gives the summit as 1,735 ft. The record keeps the list figure, and the two may describe slightly different points.

sources.title: Historical Information Currahee Mountain (GAGenWeb Stephens County pages)

notes_for_editor: Built year is the decade only ('In the 1930's'), entered as 1930. The removal is supported only by an undated genealogy-site history page (copyright notice 2004-2023), so the removal date is unknown. No source names the operating agency; the tower list gives only a GFC-style code. The county calls the mountain a popular destination; access level public is inferred from that and from its trail and race promotion. Sources also spell it 'Curahee'.
